notes_list.title: Grignard Reagent Chemistry
notes_list.basic_overview: Grignard reagents behave as strongly basic carbon nucleophiles and add to electrophilic carbon centers, especially carbonyl compounds.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Formaldehyde gives primary alcohols; aldehydes give secondary alcohols; ketones give tertiary alcohols. Esters generally require two equivalents to reach tertiary alcohols.
notes_list.examples: RMgX + carbonyl → alkoxide → alcohol after H3O+. Grignards also react with CO2 to give carboxylic acids after workup.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Strictly dry ether/THF-type conditions; water, alcohols and acids consume the reagent.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Carbon nucleophile attacks carbonyl carbon → tetrahedral magnesium alkoxide. For esters, acyl substitution gives ketone, followed by second addition.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Addition is usually fast because the carbonyl is strongly electrophilic and the reagent is highly reactive. Stoichiometry and quench control are essential.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not use Grignard with unprotected acidic OH/NH/SH groups. Steric effects can alter addition rates and product ratios.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
